articles.title: AI Call Automation Needs an Execution Ledger, Not Just a Conversation Flow
articles.excerpt: AI Call Automation Needs an Execution Ledger, Not Just a Conversation Flow An AI calling system can sound natural and still be operationally unsafe. The hardest failures are rarely bad greetings or aw…
articles.body: AI Call Automation Needs an Execution Ledger, Not Just a Conversation Flow An AI calling system can sound natural and still be operationally unsafe. The hardest failures are rarely bad greetings or awkward pauses. They are uncertain outcomes: the provider accepted a request but the application timed out; a retry launches a second call; a transfer succeeds but the workflow records failure; a customer revokes consent while a campaign queue is already populated; a transcript says an appointment was booked while the calendar write never committed. The useful design question is therefore not “Can the agent conduct this conversation?” It is: Can the business prove what was authorized, attempted, heard, changed, and reconciled for every call?
articles.author: isabelle dubuis

articles.body: This spring, a Windows hex editor I had built as a hobby went viral. A hex editor. Of all things. I’m Yutaka Hirata, a Japanese programmer and writer living in Japan. When I speak Japanese, I have a Kansai accent. You probably won’t hear it in my English, but it’s there. I’m in my fifties now, and I’m noticing more often that I don’t have the stamina I used to. Still here, though. This summer was scorching again. Having the heat drain what energy you have is no small thing. Recently, I visited Kanazawa Institute of Technology to check where I’d be taking an IT certification exam run by Japan’s Information-technology Promotion Agency. Seeing the young people on campus made me feel that perhaps I still had a few things left in me. It gave me a little energy.

articles.excerpt: The myth of the Bigfoot in GTA San Andreas might have been debunked, but it will live forever as the symbol of an exciting time in gaming.
articles.body: There is a Bigfoot in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — at least, that's what I and many others believed. Some time after the game had been released, the rumour about the new Rockstar game featuring the legendary creature spread across the internet. I remember learning about this "secret monster" from an older guy. Then I told some boys from my classroom the cool rumor I had heard about in that game our parents didn't want us to play. Word of mouth and low-resolution images shared through dial-up internet connections made GTA: San Andreas an exciting mystery.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
